finding.title: Coil fetches eagerly copy whole files and the byte-array API needs explicit scheduling/size guidance
finding.root_cause: Fetcher always materializes a ByteArray then copies it into an Okio Buffer before decoding, despite native streaming IO now being available. readByteArray is suspend but performs blocking IO on Android/iOS/Desktop without dispatcher switching. Web source is intentionally buffered; iOS also materializes NSData before ByteArray.
finding.impact: Large media produce multiple encoded-data copies plus decoder allocations, increasing latency and OOM pressure. UI callers may assume suspend means nonblocking even though source() alone documents dispatcher ownership. MEMORY labeling and lack of a supplied stable KmpFile cache key also merit integration tests.
finding.recommendation: Add native streaming adapters/URI or file mappers to Coil (or the official kotlinx-io/Okio bridge) with correct close/cancellation ownership; keep a bounded browser fallback. Document readByteArray blocking/size semantics, add decode-size guidance, and verify dataSource/keying behavior with Coil rather than inferring it.
finding.risks: Changing fetchers may affect EXIF, seek requirements, caching and thread selection. Do not label intended read-all behavior a security vulnerability; source() is already available for large-file consumers.
required_tests: Large image peak-memory benchmark by target
Stable request key and modified-file invalidation policy
evidence: Fetcher lines 25-26 allocate through readByteArray and then Buffer.write.
source() implementation and docs explicitly provide native streaming while web remains whole-buffer.
No heap benchmark or complete Coil runtime test was run, so this is an improvement with quantified benchmarks required, not a measured regression.
